metaDescription: About Rifat Sarwar: backend engineer who gets his hands dirty with ML and embedded systems, CSE graduate of IUT.
title: Serious about the work. ==Not about myself.==
paragraphs: I build backends that stay up, shrink ML models until they fit on modest hardware, and sometimes write software for machines that drive, grab and fly.
Right now I'm a Senior Software Engineer at Star Technologies, where I own backend architecture end to end. I also work on drone systems, especially the software side.

Before that I was an LLM developer at Megamind Tech (remote, Canada), fine-tuning language models with LoRA and quantizing them until they ran offline on modest hardware. At university I wrote software for IUT's Mars rover, Project Altair, which placed 6th in the world at the International Rover Challenge. Then I led Project Aero, a drone team.

I graduated from IUT in 2026 with a 3.78 CGPA and a thesis on teaching SAM3 to work underwater and on cheap hardware, all while working as an engineer. I don't recommend the schedule. I do recommend the thesis.

items.a: Yes. I build the backend, then put a model behind it. At Star Technologies that has meant a RAG pipeline over vector search and a voice assistant, both shipped as backend APIs.
The rover kept meeting rocks. Things that fly meet fewer rocks. They meet other things, which is why StarWatch carries LiDAR, optical flow and sonar.
The useful kind. It's the feeling that makes you add the Grafana alert before production adds one for you.

items.q: Do you do maths for fun?
items.a: I re-checked 115 “new best-known” records claimed by AI discovery systems, in exact rational and interval arithmetic, and found some that don't hold. So: define “fun”. (It was fun.) [The paper's here.](/#research)

Bangla Sign Language recognition. Six IMUs on an ESP32, with every finger measured relative to the wrist, so turning your whole hand changes nothing. Under rotation, the F1 score dropped by exactly zero.

items.q: What's the best way to reach you?
items.a: [The contact form](/contact) writes the email for you, and your mail app sends it to a human. The AI twin handles small talk and won't negotiate on my behalf. I checked.
